title: Phase 1b: SwiftGPUProcess orchestrator class
description: Create a Swift class (SwiftGPUProcess) that serves as the GPU process singleton/orchestrator when ENABLE_GPU_PROCESS_SWIFT is on. At this stage the class owns the call hierarchy (the @_cdecl entry forwards to it) and holds a reference to the existing C++ WebKit::GPUProcess singleton. Subsequent sub-issues translate individual initialization steps from C++ into Swift.
acceptance_criteria: SwiftGPUProcess class exists, has a singleton accessor, is the call target of the @_cdecl GPUServiceInitializer entry. Behavior identical to today: ON+OFF both build and GPUProcess.* smoke tests pass.
close_reason: SwiftGPUProcess class added as the call target of the @_cdecl entry; ON+OFF both build and pass GPUProcess smoke tests

title: Phase 4: Drop unused C++ chunks behind ENABLE_GPU_PROCESS_SWIFT
description: Once all messages and ancillary code are Swift, audit the C++ files in Source/WebKit/GPUProcess (and supporting shared code) and gate or remove the C++ versions that are no longer referenced from any Swift-built GPU process. End state: no C++ left in the GPU process build when ENABLE_GPU_PROCESS_SWIFT=ON.

title: Phase 3: Convert GPU process IPC message handlers to Swift
description: One message handler at a time, replace each C++ message receiver in the GPU process with a Swift equivalent. Order chosen via the identify-swift-candidates skill (simplest, smallest attack surface, fewest cross-process dependencies first). Each conversion is its own sub-issue.
close_reason: Phase 3 epic remains the umbrella; per-signature subtasks tracked separately. The completion-handler subtask is being broken out into OpenSource-* (next bd create)

title: Phase 2: Convert GPUProcess ancillary (non-IPC) C++ to Swift
description: Identify everything in Source/WebKit/GPUProcess and its dependencies that is NOT IPC message dispatch (initialization, sandboxing, process state, preference handling, session parameters, RemoteSharedResourceCache, shutdown, etc.) and convert it to Swift while keeping line-for-line structural correspondence with the C++. Break this into many sub-issues.
close_reason: Phase 2 epic stays open conceptually but for the GPU process specifically there's little non-IPC ancillary code; Phase 3 IPC-handler work absorbs the practical scope

title: Phase 1: Swift GPU process entry point skeleton
description: Create a Swift entry point for the GPU process that, when ENABLE_GPU_PROCESS_SWIFT is enabled, replaces GPUServiceEntryPoint.mm with a Swift entry point. At this stage the Swift code should immediately delegate to the existing C++ WebKit::GPUProcess via the existing XPCServiceInitializer<WebKit::GPUProcess, ...> mechanism. Everything else stays C++.
acceptance_criteria: When ENABLE_GPU_PROCESS_SWIFT=ON the GPU service launches via a Swift entry point and remains fully functional (TestWebKitAPI parity); when ENABLE_GPU_PROCESS_SWIFT=OFF nothing changes.
close_reason: Swift @_cdecl GPUServiceInitializer wraps existing C++ impl; ON+OFF both build and pass GPUProcess smoke tests

title: Phase 0: Add ENABLE_GPU_PROCESS_SWIFT feature flag
description: Define the ENABLE_GPU_PROCESS_SWIFT cmake feature flag (analogous to ENABLE_BACK_FORWARD_LIST_SWIFT) and ensure WebKit builds with the flag both ON and OFF on macOS, with TestWebKitAPI passing the same set of tests in both configurations. The flag does nothing at this stage.
design: Mirror the ENABLE_BACK_FORWARD_LIST_SWIFT pattern: define the option in Source/cmake/WebKitFeatures.cmake, set ON in Source/cmake/OptionsMac.cmake via SET_AND_EXPOSE_TO_BUILD, mark SWIFT_REQUIRED ON if the flag is set in WebKitFeatures.cmake.
acceptance_criteria: Flag defined in WebKitFeatures.cmake; enabled by default on Mac in OptionsMac.cmake; WebKit builds both with the flag ON and OFF; TestWebKitAPI passes the same set of tests in both configurations.
close_reason: Long since done. ENABLE_GPU_PROCESS_SWIFT cmake flag is defined and ON by default on Mac. Build green ON+OFF; smoke tests pass on both. Re-applied here after move of .beads to the worktree.
